subproblem.title: Integral formula T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R for an integer multiplicity triple
subproblem.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) : IMRep U n, and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n: a C^∞ n-form on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U). Let μ_R = R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. Then the function x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ_R-integrable, and R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) equals ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ_R(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Integrable (fun x => R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x)) R.measure ∧ R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) = ∫ x, R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂R.measure

Source: step 2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 (‡) and 3.2(3)). The parent bounds the integrand with the Euclidean bound of its step 1. Here the same bound is used in operator-norm form, which avoids the Cauchy–Binet computation.
Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, ν := μHE[n].restrict M = Hⁿ⌞M, μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity (x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞)), f(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)), K := tsupport ω. For an n-covector α, ‖α‖ is its operator norm as a continuous alternating map.
1. ω is C^∞, hence continuous, and has compact support. So K is compact, closed and Borel, and K ⊆ U because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
2. θ is measurable (R.measurable_mult; ℕ carries the discrete σ-algebra), so x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ≥0) is measurable. A measure with a density is absolutely continuous, so μ ≪ ν (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous).
3. (Measurability.) ξ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable since μ ≪ ν. ω is continuous, hence strongly measurable. Evaluation Λₙ × Λⁿ → ℝ, (ζ, α) ↦ ζ(α), is continuous (bounded bilinear; isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.continuous). So f is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).
4. (Pointwise bound.)
 - By R.orients, for ν-a.e. x (hence μ-a.e. x) there are an orthonormal family τ and s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(x)(α) = s·α(τ) for all α. Then |f(x)| = |ω(x)(τ)| ≤ ‖ω(x)‖·∏_j ‖τ_j‖ = ‖ω(x)‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
 - Since ω is continuous with compact support, there is C with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).
 - If x ∉ K then ω(x) = 0, so f(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0.
 Hence |f| ≤ C·1_K μ-a.e.
5. (Finiteness.) Since K is measurable, μ(K) = ∫_K θ dν = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ. This is finite by R.locallyIntegrable_mult, as K is compact and K ⊆ U. So C·1_K is μ-integrable, and by step 3 and domination (Integrable.mono'), f is μ-integrable.
6. (Integral identity.) For measurable g : ℝ^P → ℝ≥0 and any function h, ∫ h d(ν.withDensity g) = ∫ g(x)·h(x) dν(x). This is integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul and needs no integrability hypothesis. Take g = θ, noting (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞) = ((θ(x) : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0∞). Then
 ∫ f dμ = ∫ θ(x)·f(x) dν(x) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) = R.action ω.
 Together with step 5 this proves both claims. (A machine-checked Lean proof of exactly this argument exists: /tmp/imrep-ms-decomp/C2Check.lean.)

μ_R-a.e. |f| ≤ ‖ω‖ ≤ C·1_{spt ω}, because ξ(x) = ±ev_τ with τ orthonormal.
μ_R(spt ω) = ∫_{M∩spt ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult, so f is integrable.
∫ f dμ_R = ∫_M θ f dHⁿ = R.action ω by the withDensity integral formula.

subproblem.title: Lusin's theorem for covector fields on ℝ^P (compact form)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers and μ a measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra). Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be measurable with μ(A) < ∞, f : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (Covector (Euclid P) n) μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and ε > 0 real. Then there is a compact K ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ K) < ε on which f is continuous (ContinuousOn f K).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (ε : ℝ), MeasurableSet A → μ A ≠ ∞ → AEStronglyMeasurable f μ → 0 < ε → ∃ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ A ∧ μ (A \ K) < ENNReal.ofReal ε ∧ ContinuousOn f K
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4(a) of the parent proof, which cites Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17). Lusin's continuity theorem is not in the pinned Mathlib, which has only the Lusin–Souslin and Lusin separation theorems. So the standard proof is given, in the compact, vector-valued form used by the parent.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n is a finite-dimensional real normed space, hence a separable metric space with a countable basis of open sets. Give Λ its Borel σ-algebra.
1. (Measurable modification.) Since f is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, there is a strongly measurable f' with f = f' μ-a.e. f' is a pointwise limit of simple functions with values in the metrizable space Λ, so it is Borel measurable. The set {f ≠ f'} is μ-null, so it lies in a measurable μ-null set Z (exists_measurable_superset_of_null). Put A₀ := A ∖ Z. Then A₀ ⊆ A is measurable, μ(A ∖ A₀) ≤ μ(Z) = 0, and f = f' on A₀.
2. (Inner regularity.) ν := μ.restrict A₀ is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, since ν(ℝ^P) = μ(A₀) ≤ μ(A) < ∞. ℝ^P is a Polish space, so ν is inner regular by compact sets (Ulam's theorem; in Mathlib, finite measures on completely metrizable second-countable spaces are InnerRegular, see MeasureTheory/Measure/RegularityCompacts.lean). Hence for every measurable B ⊆ A₀ and η > 0 there is a compact C ⊆ B with μ(B ∖ C) = ν(B ∖ C) < η.
3. (Compact pieces.) Let (O_k)_{k∈ℕ} be a countable basis of the topology of Λ, and S_k := f'^{-1}(O_k), which is measurable. By step 2 choose compact sets C_k ⊆ A₀ ∩ S_k and D_k ⊆ A₀ ∖ S_k with
 μ((A₀ ∩ S_k) ∖ C_k) < ε·2^{−k−3} and μ((A₀ ∖ S_k) ∖ D_k) < ε·2^{−k−3}.
 Let E_k := C_k ∪ D_k, a compact subset of A₀. Since A₀ ∖ E_k ⊆ ((A₀ ∩ S_k) ∖ C_k) ∪ ((A₀ ∖ S_k) ∖ D_k), μ(A₀ ∖ E_k) < ε·2^{−k−2}.
4. (The compact set.) K := ⋂_k E_k is closed and contained in the compact set E_0, so K is compact, and K ⊆ A₀ ⊆ A. As A ∖ K ⊆ (A ∖ A₀) ∪ ⋃_k (A₀ ∖ E_k), countable subadditivity gives μ(A ∖ K) ≤ 0 + Σ_k ε·2^{−k−2} = ε/2 < ε.
5. (Continuity.) Fix k.
 - If x ∈ K and f'(x) ∈ O_k, then x ∈ S_k, so x ∉ D_k because D_k ∩ S_k = ∅.
 - Conversely, if x ∈ K ∖ D_k, then x ∈ E_k ∖ D_k ⊆ C_k ⊆ S_k.
 Hence K ∩ f'^{-1}(O_k) = K ∖ D_k, which is relatively open in K because D_k is closed. Since (O_k) is a basis, the restriction f'|_K is continuous (IsTopologicalBasis.continuous_iff on the subtype K). As f = f' on K ⊆ A₀, f is continuous on K, i.e. ContinuousOn f K.
proof_key_steps: Replace f by a Borel modification f' and remove a measurable null set Z: A₀ = A ∖ Z.
μ restricted to A₀ is a finite Borel measure on the Polish space ℝ^P, hence inner regular by compact sets.
For a countable basis (O_k) of Λⁿ, choose compact C_k ⊆ A₀ ∩ f'^{-1}O_k and D_k ⊆ A₀ ∖ f'^{-1}O_k with defects < ε·2^{−k−3}.
K = ⋂_k (C_k ∪ D_k) is compact, K ⊆ A, and μ(A ∖ K) ≤ ε/2.
K ∩ f'^{-1}O_k = K ∖ D_k is relatively open in K, so f = f' is continuous on K.

Summable measure losses and relatively open basis preimages give exactly the claimed compact set and continuity, without additional measure hypotheses.

subproblem.title: Smooth unit-norm approximation of a continuous covector field on a compact set
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (K V : Set (Euclid P)) (β : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (δ : ℝ), IsCompact K → IsOpen V → K ⊆ V → ContinuousOn β K → (∀ x ∈ K, covectorEuclideanNorm (β x) ≤ 1) → 0 < δ → ∃ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - β x) ≤ δ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4(c)–(d) of the parent proof (Tietze extension, radial retraction onto the unit ball of |·|, cut-off, mollification). They are packaged so that only the estimate on K is recorded.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n with operator norm ‖·‖; |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm; 𝓘 is the set of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P, and e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}).
0. If K = ∅, then ω := 0 works: it is smooth with compact support, tsupport 0 = ∅ ⊆ V, and |0| = 0. Assume K ≠ ∅ from now on.
1. (The norm |·|.) Let 𝒜 : Λ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P) be the linear map with 𝒜(α)_I := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing and 0 otherwise. It is continuous (finite dimension), and by the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm, |α| = ‖𝒜(α)‖. Consequently:
 (N1) |·| is continuous;
 (N2) |cα| = |c|·|α|;
 (N3) |α + α'| ≤ |α| + |α'|;
 (N4) |∫ g dm| ≤ ∫ |g| dm for every finite measure m and m-integrable g : ℝ^P → Λ, since 𝒜 commutes with the Bochner integral and the norm of an integral is at most the integral of the norm;
 (N5) |α| ≤ C₀‖α‖ with C₀ := (#𝓘)^{1/2}, because |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖.
2. (Tietze.) K is closed and β|_K is continuous. Λ is a finite-dimensional real vector space, so the Tietze extension theorem gives a continuous β̃ : ℝ^P → Λ with β̃ = β on K (Mathlib ContinuousMap.exists_restrict_eq with the TietzeExtension instance RCLike.instTietzeExtensionTVS for finite-dimensional real spaces, or coordinatewise in a basis).
3. (Retraction.) Put ρ(α) := max(1, |α|)^{−1}·α. ρ is continuous by (N1). By (N2), |ρ(α)| = |α|/max(1, |α|) ≤ 1, and ρ(α) = α when |α| ≤ 1.
4. (Cut-off.) K is compact and V open, so there is r > 0 with cthickening(2r, K) := {x : dist(x, K) ≤ 2r} ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put χ(x) := max(0, 1 − dist(x, K)/r). χ is continuous, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on K. Since χ(x) = 0 when dist(x, K) ≥ r, support χ ⊆ thickening(r, K) := {x : dist(x, K) < r}.
5. (Continuous unit field.) g := χ·(ρ ∘ β̃) is continuous, with support g ⊆ thickening(r, K) and tsupport g ⊆ cthickening(r, K), which is compact (K compact, ℝ^P proper). Moreover |g(x)| = χ(x)·|ρ(β̃(x))| ≤ 1 for all x. For x ∈ K, g(x) = ρ(β(x)) = β(x), because χ = 1 and |β| ≤ 1 there.
6. (Mollification.) g is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous. Choose s with 0 < s ≤ r such that ‖g(y) − g(x)‖ ≤ δ/(C₀ + 1) whenever dist(y, x) < s. Let φ ≥ 0 be a smooth bump function with ∫ φ dx = 1 and support φ = B_s(0) (Mathlib ContDiffBump (0 : ℝ^P) with rOut = s, normed for Lebesgue measure). Define ω := φ ⋆ g, ω(x) = ∫ φ(t)·g(x − t) dt (Bochner integral in Λ).
 (i) ω is C^∞: it is the convolution of a C^∞ compactly supported kernel with a continuous, hence locally integrable, function (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
 (ii) support ω ⊆ support φ + support g ⊆ B_s(0) + thickening(r, K) ⊆ thickening(2r, K), using s ≤ r (support_convolution_subset). Hence tsupport ω ⊆ cthickening(2r, K) ⊆ V, a compact set. So ω is C^∞ with compact support (IsTestForm ω) and tsupport ω ⊆ V.
 (iii) For every x, by (N4), φ ≥ 0, |g| ≤ 1 and ∫ φ = 1: |ω(x)| ≤ ∫ φ(t)·|g(x − t)| dt ≤ ∫ φ(t) dt = 1.
 (iv) For every x, φ(t) = 0 unless |t| < s, and ∫ φ = 1. So ‖ω(x) − g(x)‖ = ‖∫ φ(t)·(g(x − t) − g(x)) dt‖ ≤ δ/(C₀ + 1) (ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le). By (N5), |ω(x) − g(x)| ≤ C₀·δ/(C₀ + 1) ≤ δ.
7. For x ∈ K, g(x) = β(x) by step 5, so |ω(x) − β(x)| ≤ δ by 6(iv). Together with 6(i)–(iii), ω has all the required properties.
proof_key_steps: |·| = ‖𝒜(·)‖ for the coefficient map 𝒜, so |·| is a continuous norm with |∫ g| ≤ ∫ |g| and |α| ≤ C₀‖α‖.
Extend β|_K continuously (Tietze), retract radially onto {|·| ≤ 1}, and multiply by the cut-off χ = max(0, 1 − dist(·, K)/r): g is continuous, |g| ≤ 1, g = β on K, tsupport g ⊆ cthickening(r, K).
Mollify with a normalized smooth bump of radius s ≤ r: the result is C^∞ with tsupport ⊆ cthickening(2r, K) ⊆ V and |ω| ≤ 1 by convexity.
Uniform continuity gives |ω − g| ≤ δ everywhere, and g = β on K.

subproblem.title: Support of a current from a mass–measure identity
subproblem.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), and μ a measure on ℝ^P with M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P (M_W(T) = T.massOn W). Then spt T = U ∩ spt μ, where spt T = T.support (Simon 6.2.11) and spt μ = μ.support.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = μ W) → T.support = U ∩ μ.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.11–2.12). In 5(b) the parent shows T(ω) = 0 from the integral formula. Here the same vanishing follows from the mass identity alone (step 2), so the lemma holds for an arbitrary measure μ.
Notation: |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm. M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal T(ω) over admissible ω, i.e. ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. spt T = T.support = U ∖ Z_T, where Z_T is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T vanishing on W (T(ω) = 0 for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W). x ∈ spt μ iff μ(N) > 0 for every neighbourhood N of x (Measure.mem_support_iff_forall).
1. (Homogeneity and continuity of |·|.) From the defining formula |α| = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}:
 - |cα| = (Σ_I c²·α(e_I)²)^{1/2} = |c|·|α| for c ∈ ℝ;
 - α ↦ |α| is continuous, being the square root of a finite sum of squares of the continuous evaluations α ↦ α(e_I).
2. (Zero mass forces vanishing.) Suppose M_W(T) = 0 and let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
 - x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous with compact support (|0| = 0), so there is a real C with |ω(x)| ≤ C for all x.
 - Put a := (max(C, 0) + 1)^{−1} > 0. For s ∈ {a, −a}, sω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport(sω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, and |sω(x)| = a·|ω(x)| ≤ a·(max(C, 0) + 1) = 1. So sω is admissible.
 - Hence ofReal(s·T(ω)) = ofReal(T(sω)) ≤ M_W(T) = 0, i.e. s·T(ω) ≤ 0.
 With s = a and s = −a this gives T(ω) = 0. So T vanishes on W.
3. (spt T ⊆ U ∩ spt μ.) Let x ∈ spt T, so x ∈ U and x ∉ Z_T. Suppose x ∉ spt μ: some neighbourhood N of x has μ(N) = 0. Choose r₁, r₂ > 0 with B_{r₁}(x) ⊆ N and B_{r₂}(x) ⊆ U (U is open), and let r := min(r₁, r₂)/2 and W := B_r(x).
 - W is open. closure W ⊆ B̄_r(x) ⊆ B_{r₂}(x) ⊆ U, and closure W is compact as a closed subset of the compact ball B̄_r(x).
 - M_W(T) = μ(W) ≤ μ(N) = 0, so T vanishes on W by step 2.
 Thus W is one of the sets forming Z_T, so x ∈ W ⊆ Z_T, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ U ∩ spt μ.
4. (U ∩ spt μ ⊆ spt T.) Let x ∈ U ∩ spt μ and suppose x ∈ Z_T, i.e. x ∈ W for some open W on which T vanishes.
 - Every admissible ω for M_W(T) has tsupport ω ⊆ W, so T(ω) = 0. Hence M_W(T), a supremum of values ofReal 0 = 0, equals 0, and μ(W) = M_W(T) = 0.
 - But W is an open neighbourhood of x ∈ spt μ, so μ(W) > 0.
 This contradiction shows x ∉ Z_T, so x ∈ U ∖ Z_T = spt T.
5. Steps 3 and 4 give T.support = U ∩ μ.support. (A machine-checked Lean proof of exactly this argument, axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only, is in /tmp/imrep-ms-decomp/Sanity.lean.)
proof_key_steps: |cα| = |c|·|α|, and α ↦ |α| is continuous.
M_W(T) = 0 implies T vanishes on W: rescale ω by ±a so that it is admissible.
If x ∈ spt T but μ vanishes on a neighbourhood of x, a small ball W around x has M_W(T) = 0, so x ∈ Z_T: contradiction.
If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ lay in a zero region W, then μ(W) = M_W(T) = 0, contradicting x ∈ spt μ.

subproblem.title: Euclidean coefficient-norm duality for unit simple n-vectors (Cauchy–Binet)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ L : MultiVector P n →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n, ∀ (ξ : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ covectorEuclideanNorm (L ξ) ≤ 1 ∧ ξ (L ξ) = 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, §1: coordinate covectors dx^I and the pairing of Λⁿ with Λₙ). The Cauchy–Binet identity is proved inline.
Notation:
- e_0, …, e_{P−1} is the standard basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun), and v(i) is the i-th coordinate of v ∈ ℝ^P.
- Λⁿ := Covector (Euclid P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ; Λₙ := MultiVector P n = Λⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ.
- 𝓘 is the finite set of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P, and e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}).
- For α ∈ Λⁿ, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} α(e_I)²)^{1/2}. The defining sum runs over all I : Fin n → Fin P, with term α(e_I)² for strictly increasing I and 0 otherwise, so it is the same sum.
- For v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n and I ∈ 𝓘, v^I is the n×n matrix with (k, j) entry v_j(I(k)).
1. (Coordinate covectors.) For I ∈ 𝓘 let dx^I ∈ Λⁿ be dx^I(v) := det(v^I). It is n-linear and alternating in v, because the determinant is multilinear and alternating in its columns and column j, (v_j(I(k)))_k, depends linearly on v_j. It is continuous because ℝ^P is finite-dimensional. In SimonGMT (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.FormsDuality), dx^I = wedgeCovectors n (fun k ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (I k)), and wedgeCovectors_apply_det gives exactly this formula. For n = 0, dx^I is the constant covector 1, the determinant of the empty matrix.
2. (Kronecker property.) For I, J ∈ 𝓘, dx^I(e_J) = 1 if I = J and dx^I(e_J) = 0 if I ≠ J. The matrix (e_J)^I has (k, j) entry 1 if I(k) = J(j) and 0 otherwise. If I = J it is the identity matrix. If I ≠ J, the ranges differ, because a strictly increasing map Fin n → Fin P is the increasing enumeration of its range. Both ranges have n elements, so some I(k) is not in range J. Row k of (e_J)^I is then zero, and the determinant is 0.
3. (Expansion.) For every α ∈ Λⁿ and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^n: α(v) = Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} α(e_I)·dx^I(v).
 Both sides are alternating n-linear functions of v; the right side is a linear combination of the dx^I. By multilinearity, two n-linear maps on ℝ^P agree once they agree on every basis tuple e_f := (e_{f(0)}, …, e_{f(n−1)}), f : Fin n → Fin P.
 - If f is not injective, both alternating maps vanish at e_f, which has a repeated entry.
 - If f is injective, let J ∈ 𝓘 enumerate range f increasingly, and let σ be the permutation of Fin n with f = J ∘ σ. By alternation, each side at e_f equals sign(σ) times its value at e_J. At e_J the right side is Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I(e_J) = α(e_J) by step 2.
 Hence the two sides agree.
4. (Sum of squared minors; Cauchy–Binet.) For every orthonormal family τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) in ℝ^P, Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} det(τ^I)² = 1. This is the Cauchy–Binet formula det(AᵀA) = Σ_I det(A_I)² for the P×n matrix A with columns τ_j, where AᵀA = Id. Self-contained derivation:
 - Let δ_τ ∈ Λⁿ be δ_τ(v) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}. It is n-linear, alternating and continuous for the same reasons as dx^I, and equals wedgeCovectors n (fun i ↦ ⟨τ_i, ·⟩).
 - By orthonormality, δ_τ(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = det(Id) = 1.
 - δ_τ(e_I) = det(τ_i(I(j)))_{i,j} = det((τ^I)ᵀ) = det(τ^I), and dx^I(τ) = det(τ^I).
 - Step 3 with α = δ_τ and v = τ gives 1 = δ_τ(τ) = Σ_I δ_τ(e_I)·dx^I(τ) = Σ_I det(τ^I)².
5. (Proof of (a).) Let ξ, Q satisfy IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q, with orthonormal τ and sign s, so ξ(α) = s·α(τ) for all α. For α ∈ Λⁿ, step 3 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^𝓘 give
 |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| = |Σ_I α(e_I) det(τ^I)| ≤ (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}·(Σ_I det(τ^I)²)^{1/2} = |α|·1,
 using step 4.
6. (Definition of L.) For ζ ∈ Λₙ put L(ζ) := Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} ζ(dx^I)·dx^I. Each ζ ↦ ζ(dx^I) is evaluation at a fixed point, a continuous linear functional on Λₙ. So L is a finite sum of continuous linear maps Λₙ → Λⁿ, i.e. L ∈ (MultiVector P n →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n). For example, L = Σ_I (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ (dx^I)).smulRight (dx^I). L does not depend on ξ.
7. (Coefficients of L(ζ).) For J ∈ 𝓘, step 2 gives L(ζ)(e_J) = Σ_I ζ(dx^I)·dx^I(e_J) = ζ(dx^J). Hence |L(ζ)|² = Σ_{J ∈ 𝓘} ζ(dx^J)².
8. (Proof of (b) and (c).) For ξ as in step 5, ξ(dx^J) = s·dx^J(τ) = s·det(τ^J).
 - By step 7 and step 4, |L(ξ)|² = Σ_J s²·det(τ^J)² = 1, so |L(ξ)| = 1 ≤ 1.
 - By linearity of ξ, ξ(L(ξ)) = Σ_I ξ(dx^I)·ξ(dx^I) = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1.
9. (Degenerate cases need no separate treatment.)
 - For n = 0, 𝓘 consists of the empty map, e_∅ is the empty tuple, dx^∅ = 1 and |α| = |α(e_∅)|. Steps 1–8 hold verbatim.
 - If n > P, then 𝓘 = ∅ and step 4 would give 0 = 1. So ℝ^P has no orthonormal family of n vectors, the hypothesis IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q never holds, and the statement is vacuous (L = 0).
proof_key_steps: Define dx^I(v) = det(v_j(I(k)))_{k,j} (SimonGMT wedgeCovectors of coordinate projections); dx^I(e_J) = δ_IJ for strictly increasing I, J.
Expansion α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I)·dx^I(v): both sides are alternating multilinear and agree on all basis tuples.
Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1 for orthonormal τ (Cauchy–Binet), by expanding δ_τ(v) = det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩) at v = τ.
Cauchy–Schwarz gives |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ |α|.
L(ζ) = Σ_I ζ(dx^I)·dx^I is continuous linear, with |L(ξ)|² = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1 and ξ(L(ξ)) = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1.

subproblem.title: Lower mass bound μ_R(W) ≤ M_W(T) for open W
subproblem.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), and R = (M, θ, ξ) : IMRep U n with R.Represents T. Then μ_R(W) ≤ M_W(T) in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where μ_R = R.measure and M_W(T) = T.massOn W.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → R.measure W ≤ T.massOn W
subproblem.natural_proof:

0. (Duality and the good set.) Fix a continuous linear L : Λₙ → Λⁿ by dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual. Call x good if (i) |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α, (ii) |L(ξ(x))| ≤ 1, and (iii) ξ(x)(L(ξ(x))) = 1. By R.orients, for ν-a.e. x some Q has IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q, so ν-a.e. x is good, hence μ-a.e. x is good (μ ≪ ν). Choose a measurable μ-null set Z containing all bad points (exists_measurable_superset_of_null). Put β(x) := L(ξ(x)), the parent's ξ^♭. β is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: ξ is ν-a.e., hence μ-a.e., strongly measurable, and L is continuous.
1. (Finiteness, concentration.) For compact K ⊆ U, μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Also μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, because ν(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0 and M ⊆ U.
2. (Reduction to G.) G := W ∩ U is open, and μ(W) = μ(G) because μ(G) ≤ μ(W) ≤ μ(G) + μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = μ(G).
3. (Real thresholds.) By ENNReal.le_of_forall_nnreal_lt it suffices to prove r ≤ M_W(T) for every real r ≥ 0 with r < μ(G). Fix such r and choose η > 0 with r + 4η < μ(G): η := 1 if μ(G) = ∞, and η := (μ(G) − r)/5 otherwise.
4. (Inner compact approximation.) For j ∈ ℕ let G_j := B̄_j(0) ∖ {x : dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ G) < 1/(j+1)}, the closed ball minus the open 1/(j+1)-neighbourhood of ℝ^P ∖ G (empty if G = ℝ^P).
 - Each G_j is closed and bounded, hence compact; G_j ⊆ G; and G_j increases with j.
 - ⋃_j G_j = G: for x ∈ G there is ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ G. So x is outside the 1/(j+1)-neighbourhood of ℝ^P ∖ G once 1/(j+1) ≤ ε, and x ∈ G_j once also j ≥ |x|.
 By continuity of μ from below (tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop), μ(G_j) → μ(G). So there is a compact K := G_j ⊆ G with μ(K) > r + 4η, and μ(K) < ∞ by step 1 since K ⊆ U.

Then μ(K ∖ K') ≤ μ((K ∖ Z) ∖ K') + μ(Z) < η. Every x ∈ K' is good, since K' ∩ Z = ∅; in particular |β(x)| ≤ 1 on K'.
6. (Outer open approximation.) K' is compact and G open, so there is ρ > 0 with cthickening(ρ, K') ⊆ G (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). This set is compact and contained in U, so its μ-measure is finite. Consider the open sets V_j := thickening(ρ/(j+1), K') = {x : dist(x, K') < ρ/(j+1)}:
 - they decrease, contain K' and lie in cthickening(ρ, K');
 - ⋂_j V_j = K': if x ∉ K', some ball B_ε(x) misses the closed set K', so x ∉ V_j once ρ/(j+1) ≤ ε.

subproblem.title: Upper mass bound M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), and R = (M, θ, ξ) : IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = R.action ω for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Then M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) in [0, ∞] for every set W ⊆ ℝ^P. Here μ_R = R.measure, and M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm (ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof. It is stated here for an arbitrary set W: openness of W is not used, because the argument compares with μ_R(tsupport ω).
Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, ν := Hⁿ⌞M, μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity θ ≪ ν, |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm.
1. (A.e. duality bound.) Choose L by the sibling theorem dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual (unit_orientation_duality). Only its part (a) is used: if IsUnitOrientationOf ξ₀ Q, then |ξ₀(α)| ≤ |α| for all α. By R.orients, for ν-a.e. x there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. Hence for ν-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α. Since μ ≪ ν (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous, AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le), this holds for μ-a.e. x.
2. (Reduction.) T.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. By sSup_le it suffices to show ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ μ(W) for every admissible ω.
3. Fix an admissible ω and put K := tsupport ω. K is compact, K ⊆ U (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U)) and K ⊆ W (admissibility). K is closed, hence measurable, so by withDensity_apply and restrict_restrict, μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult).
4. By R.Represents T and the sibling theorem dor_ims_action_eq_integral (action_integral_formula), T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫ f dμ, where f(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable.
5. (Pointwise comparison.) For μ-a.e. x:
 - if x ∈ K, then f(x) ≤ |f(x)| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1, by step 1 and admissibility;
 - if x ∉ K, then ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so f(x) = 0.
 So f ≤ 1_K μ-a.e., and 1_K is μ-integrable because μ(K) < ∞. By monotonicity of the integral (integral_mono_ae, integral_indicator_one), T(ω) = ∫ f dμ ≤ ∫ 1_K dμ = μ(K).toReal.
6. Hence ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ ofReal(μ(K).toReal) = μ(K) ≤ μ(W). The equality uses μ(K) < ∞; the inequality uses K ⊆ W and monotonicity of μ, valid for any W. Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M_W(T) ≤ μ(W). (Machine-checked from the sibling types: /tmp/imrep-ms-decomp/Sanity.lean.)
